submission.justification: D3 at 30% coverage is the best choice among designs that pass the thermal-cycling requirement. It gives about 38.7 PE/MeV, against 25.1 for D1 at 30%. D2 has the highest light yield (about 52–54 PE/MeV at 30%) but fails thermal cycling, with a 30% failure fraction against a 5% limit. It is excluded because failed modules cannot be replaced. Caveat: the reliability evidence is weak. The batch was 40 modules per design, so the reported failure fractions of 2% for D3 and 0.5% for D1 do not match whole-module counts (0.8 and 0.2 modules). Even zero failures in 40 modules gives a 95% upper bound of about 7.5%, which is above the 5% limit. So the 5% requirement for D3 is met by the point estimate but is not statistically demonstrated. I recommend a larger thermal-cycling batch for D3 before the design is frozen. D1 is the fallback if D3 reliability does not hold up, but it costs about a third of the light.

requirements.evidence: D3 at 30% gives 38.7 PE/MeV, the highest among the thermally passing designs. D2 gives more (54.4) but is excluded.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the designs in candidate_specs.md
At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: The D3 point estimate is 2%, which is below the limit. The batch of 40 cannot show this at 95% confidence, because the rule-of-three bound is 7.5% even with zero failures. The reported fractions are also not integer counts out of 40. D2 clearly fails at 30%.
30% is within range and is at the feedthrough maximum of 30%. D3 shows no saturation.
